routes.label: Fix the floor on each unit interval

question: For every real number \(x,\) let \(\lfloor x\rfloor\) denote the greatest integer not exceeding \(x,\) and let \[f(x)=\lfloor x\rfloor\left(2014^{\,x-\lfloor x\rfloor}-1\right).\] The set of all numbers \(x\) such that \(1\le x\lt2014\) and \(f(x)\le1\) is a union of disjoint intervals. What is the sum of the lengths of those intervals?
solution:
On each interval between consecutive integers, the floor is constant. Write
\[
x=j+t,\qquad j=1,2,\ldots,2013,\quad 0\le t<1.
\]
Then \(\lfloor x\rfloor=j\), and the condition becomes
\[
j(2014^t-1)\le1
\iff 2014^t\le\frac{j+1}{j}.
\]
Since \(2014>1\), its exponential function is increasing. Therefore the allowed values of \(t\) are
\[
0\le t\le L_j,
\qquad L_j=\log_{2014}\frac{j+1}{j}.
\]
Because \(1<(j+1)/j\le2<2014\), we have \(0<L_j<1\). Thus each unit interval contributes exactly the closed interval \([j,j+L_j]\). These intervals are disjoint, and all lie within \(1\le x<2014\).

Their total length is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{j=1}^{2013}L_j
&=\sum_{j=1}^{2013}
\left(\log_{2014}(j+1)-\log_{2014}j\right)\\
&=\log_{2014}2014-\log_{2014}1\\
&=1.
\end{aligned}
\]
Every intermediate logarithm cancels, leaving only the first and last endpoints. The requested sum is \(\boxed{1}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
